title: Unit 6: Customary and Local Governance Systems & Peace Making
content:
ውድ! የEthioFresh ቤተሰቦች! ✋✨
እንኳን ወደ Social Anthropology Unit 6 (Part 1) ትምህርታችን በሰላም መጣችሁ! በባለፈው ምዕራፍ ስለ ብሔረሰብ፣ ብሔራዊ ማንነት እና መልቲካልቸራሊዝም በስፋት ተነጋግረናል:: ዛሬ ደግሞ ወሳኝ እና ጥልቅ የሆነውን Unit 6: Customary and Local Governance Systems and Peace Making እንጀምራለን! ከክፍል 6.1 (Indigenous and Local Governance) እስከ 6.2 (Indigenous Institutions of Conflict Resolution) ያሉትን ሀሳቦች እንመለከታለን:: ዘና ብላችሁ፣ ተከታተሉኝ! 😊💡


1. INTRODUCTION TO UNIT SIX

In Unit 5, we discussed theories related to ethnicity, ethnic groups, ethnic identity, and theories of ethnic identity. In Unit 6, we will discuss issues related to customary and local governance and peacemaking in the Ethiopian setting. Specifically, we will discuss the role of customary institutions in settling intra- and inter-ethnic conflicts; women's role and women's institutions in conflict resolution and peacemaking; and the main features of legal pluralism in Ethiopia. Student participation is very important as the modular course employs a student-centered approach.

Content of the Unit:
• Indigenous and local governance
• Institutions of intra- and inter-ethnic conflict resolution
• Structures of indigenous justice systems
• Strengths and limitations of indigenous conflict resolution institutions
• Women's role in conflict resolution and peacemaking
• Legal pluralism: interaction between customary and state legal systems

👉 የምዕራፉ አጠቃላይ መንደደርያ፡
በዚህ ምዕራፍ ውስጥ በኢትዮጵያ የተለያዩ ማህበረሰቦች ዘንድ የሚገኙ ባህላዊና የአካባቢ የPlatform እና የአስተዳደር ስርዓቶችን (Customary & Local Governance System)፣ የሰላም ግንባታ እና የግብረ-ግጭት አፈታት መንገዶችን እንማራለን:: ትምህርቱ የሀገር በቀል የህግ ስርዓቶች እና የመንግስት ህግ እንዴት አብረው እንደሚሰሩ (Legal Pluralism) እና የሴቶች አስተዋፅኦ ምን እንደሚመስል በዝርዝር ያቀርባል::አብሮነታችሁ አይለዬን👇


6.1: INDIGENOUS AND LOCAL GOVERNANCE

Indigenous systems of governance have widely been employed to maintain social order across Ethiopian regions. The role of indigenous governance was indispensable before the advent of the modern state system. Anthropologists have been studying indigenous systems of governance in Ethiopia and other parts of Africa. Some of the indigenous systems of governance have been well-studied while many others have got little attention by scholars. Understanding indigenous systems of governance helps us know our cultures in a better way. It will also help us enhance inter-cultural understanding and smooth relationships among different ethnic/cultural groups. We do not have space to take examples from every region and culture. Hence, we have outlined some examples of indigenous systems of governance.

👉 ዘመናዊ የመንግስት አስተዳደር ስርዓት (Modern state system) ከመምጣቱ በፊት፣ ሀገር በቀል የሆኑ የአስተዳደር ስርዓቶች በማህበረሰቡ ውስጥ ሰላምና ስርዓትን ለማስከበር ከፍተኛ ሚና ተጫውተዋል:: እነዚህን ስርዓቶች መረዳታችን ባህላችንን እንድናውቅና በልዩ ልዩ የብሔር/የባህል ቡድኖች መካከል መልካም ግንኙነት እንዲኖር ይረዳል::


1. THE OROMO GADAA SYSTEM

The Gadaa of the Oromo is one of the well-studied indigenous systems of governance. Various scholars have been studying the Oromo Gadaa since the 1950s. Paul Baxter, Eike Haberland, and Asmerom Legesse are some of the scholars who studied the Oromo Gadaa. Asmerom, a famous anthropologist, is widely known for his ethnographic studies on the Oromo political system. He published a lot on the Gadaa system, particularly focusing on the Borena Oromo. The following are two of his books on Oromo indigenous political system:
• Gadaa: Three Approaches to the Study of African Society, published in 1973
• Oromo Democracy: An Indigenous Political System, published in 2000

Structure and Features of Gadaa:
• The Gadaa system is 'an age grading institution of the Oromo that has a complex system of administration, law making and dispute settlement' (Pankhurst and Getachew 2008, xiv).
• Gadaa is a highly celebrated institution of governance and dispute settlement among the Oromo people, widely mentioned as an egalitarian (democratic) system of governance.
• Political power is transferred from one generation set (Luuba) to another every eight years.
• Gadaa officials such as the Abba Gada and Abba Seera (father of law) serve for eight years and leave their position to the new generation of Gadaa officials.
• The Gadaa system involves a continuous process of law making and revision with rooms for wider participation of the people.
• Gumi gaayo: A law making assembly of the Borana Oromo held every eight years to revise, adapt, make, and publicize customary law (seera) and custom (aadaa).
• Yaa'iiharaa: The law making assembly equivalent to gumigaayo among the Waliso Oromo, held every eight years.
• Gadaa is an indigenous system of governance, conflict resolution, and peacemaking.
• The institution of Jaarsa Biyyaa (literally: elders of the soil/land) handles council of elders functions for settling conflicts and restoring peace.

👉 የኦሮሞ ገዳ ስርዓት ዋና ነጥቦች፡
• የገዳ ስርዓት በእድሜ እርከን (Age grading institution) ላይ የተመሰረተ ዲሞክራሲያዊ (Egalitarian) የአስተዳደር እና የህግ አውጪነት ስርዓት ነው::
• ፖለቲካዊ ስልጣን በየ 8 አመቱ ከአንድ ትውልድ እርከን (Luuba) ወደ ሌላው ይተላለፋል::
• Abba Gadaa (የስርዓቱ መሪ) እና Abba Seera (የህግ አባት) ለ8 አመታት ያገለግላሉ::
• ህግ የማውጣትና የማሻሻል ጉባኤዎች በየ8 አመቱ ይካሄዳሉ፡ በቦረና Gumi Gaayo ሲባል፣ በወሊሶ ኦሮሞ ደግሞ Yaa'iiharaa ይባላል::
• Jaarsa Biyyaa (የሀገር ሽማግሌዎች) ግጭቶችን በሰላም የመፍታት ሚና ይጫወታሉ::

💡 Exam Hint: በፈተና ላይ የአስመሮም ለገሰ (Asmerom Legesse) መጻህፍት፣ የስልጣን ዘመን (8 years)፣ እና የህግ አውጪ ጉባኤዎች ስም (Gumi Gaayo / Yaa'iiharaa) በ 'Multiple Choice' መጠየቃቸው አይቀሬ ነው!


2. THE GEDEO BAALLE SYSTEM

The Gedeo of southern Ethiopia have an indigenous system of governance called Baalle. The Baalle and the Gaada system of the Oromo have some similarities. For example, both have age grading system and exercise periodic transfer of power (i.e., every eight years). The role of religion is high in the two indigenous systems of governance. Moreover, the customary law of the Gedeo is called Seera. The Ya'a, the general assembly, is the highest body of the Gedeo indigenous system of governance. The Baalle is a complex system which has three administrative hierarchies: Abba Gada, Roga (traditional leader next the Abba Gada), and two levels of council of elders known as Hulla Hayyicha and Songo Hayyicha. The Abba Gada is the leader of the Baalle.

Hierarchy and Functions of Baalle:
• Conflicts are resolved by the Songo Hayyicha at village level.
• When disputes are not settled at the village level, cases can be referred to the Hulla Hayyicha and finally to the Abba Gada.
• Major institutions include: Ya'a (general assembly), Seera (customary law), Abba Gada, and council of elders (Getachew, 2014).

👉 የጌዴኦ ባሌ (Baalle) ስርዓት ዋና ነጥቦች፡
• ከኦሮሞ ገዳ ስርዓት ጋር ይመሳሰላል (በእድሜ እርከን እና በየ8 አመቱ ስልጣን በማስተላለፍ)::
• Seera: የጌዴኦ ባህላዊ ህግ ነው:: Ya'a: የጌዴኦ ህዝብ የበላይ ጠቅላላ ጉባኤ ነው::
• የስልጣን ተዋረድ፡ Abba Gada (ዋና መሪ) ➡️ Roga (ከአባ ገዳ ቀጥሎ ያለ መሪ) ➡️ Hulla Hayyicha (የሽማግሌዎች ምክር ቤት) ➡️ Songo Hayyicha (በመንደር ደረጃ ያለ የሽማግሌዎች ምክር ቤት)::

😄 ቅምሻ ቀልድ: በጌዴኦ ባሌ ስርዓት ውስጥ መዝለል የለም! ጉዳይህ ከመንደሩ Songo Hayyicha ተነስተህ ካልተጨረሰ ነው ወደ Abba Gada የሚሄደው፤ ልክ እንደ modern court appeal ማለት ነው! 😂


3. DERE WOGA OF THE GAMO

The Gamo are among Omotic peoples of southern Ethiopia. Unlike their neighboring people such as Wolayta and Dawro, the Gamo did not have a centralized political system. The Gamo people were organized into several local administrations locally known as deres. According to anthropological findings, most of deres were governed by a ka'o (king) and halaqa (elected leader). The Gamo indigenous system of governance embraces the dere woga (customary law) and the dubusha assemblies.

Key Institutions & Beliefs:
• Dere dubusha: The highest body of indigenous governance and general assembly of local people, responsible for making/revising customary laws and resolving major disputes.
• Hierarchies of Dubusha: 1) dere dubusha (at the top), 2) sub-dere dubusha (at the middle level), and 3) guta/neighborhood dubusha (at the village level). Minor cases and disputes are resolved by dere cima (council of elders).
• Belief System Integration: Embedded in Gamo belief system. Telling a lie and hiding the truth, especially at dubusha assemblies, are considered violations of taboo leading to spiritual pollution, lack of fertility, illness, and death of humans and livestock. Fear of misfortunes compels people to reveal the truth at dubusha assemblies.

👉 የጋሞ ደሬ ወጋ (Dere Woga) ዋና ነጥቦች፡
• ጋሞዎች እንደ ወላይታና ዳውሮ ማዕከላዊ ፖለቲካዊ ስርዓት አልነበራቸውም፤ በብዙ Deres (የአካባቢ አስተዳደሮች) የተዋቀሩ ነበሩ::
• ይመሩ የነበረው በ Ka'o (ንጉስ) እና በ Halaqa (የተመረጠ መሪ) ነው::
• Dere Woga: ባህላዊ ህጋቸው ሲሆን፣ Dubusha: ደግሞ ባህላዊ የህዝብ ስብሰባ/ችሎት ነው::
• የDubusha ደረጃዎች፡ Dere dubusha (በላይኛ ደረጃ) ➡️ Sub-dere dubusha (በመካከለኛ ደረጃ) ➡️ Guta dubusha (በመንደር ደረጃ)::
• ሃይማኖታዊ እምነት፡ በDubusha ፊት ውሸት መናገር ነውር (Taboo) እና መንፈሳዊ እድፈትን ያመጣል ተብሎ ስለሚታመን ህዝቡ እውነቱን ብቻ ይናገራል::


6.2: INDIGENOUS INSTITUTIONS OF CONFLICT RESOLUTION AND PEACEMAKING

Conflict is a common phenomenon in human societies and communities. Human beings develop different institutions and mechanisms to resolve conflicts and restore peace and social order. More than 80 ethnic and cultural groups live together in Ethiopia. Each ethnic group has its own institutions of conflict resolution and peacemaking. Regardless of cross-cultural diversity, most ethnic/cultural groups in Ethiopia have similar conflict resolution institutions. The basic ones are customary (unwritten) laws, customary courts, and council of elders. Although women play a significant role in conflict resolution, they are marginalized from mainstream institutions in most cultural settings.

Two Main Types of Conflict Resolution Institutions:
1. Intra-ethnic conflict resolution institutions: Address conflicts between individuals and groups (e.g., clans) within the same ethnic group.
2. Inter-ethnic conflict resolution institutions: Resolve conflicts between individuals and groups of different ethnic groups.

👉 የግጭት አፈታት ተቋማት ምደባ፡
በኢትዮጵያ ከ80 በላይ ብሔረሰቦች ያሉ ቢሆንም፣ የባህላዊ ግጭት አፈታት መንገዶቻቸው ተመሳሳይነት አላቸው:: ግጭት አፈታት በሁለት ይከፈላል፡
1. Intra-ethnic: በአንድ ብሔር ውስጥ ባሉ አባላት/ጎሳዎች መካከል የሚፈጠር ግጭት አፈታት::
2. Inter-ethnic: በተለያዩ ብሔሮች መካከል የሚፈጠር ግጭት አፈታት::


6.2.1: INTRA-ETHNIC CONFLICT RESOLUTION INSTITUTIONS & COMPONENTS

Intra-ethnic conflict resolution institutions embrace three major components across Ethiopian cultures:
1. Customary law
2. Council of elders
3. Customary courts or assemblies

Component 1: Customary Law
Customary law refers to a body of rules, norms, and a set of moral values that serve as a wider framework for human conduct and social interactions. Most are available orally, though some have been published in written forms.
• Examples of Customary Laws:
- Sera of the Sidama
- Dere woga of the Gamo
- Seera Addaa of the Oromo
- Ye Siltie Serra of the Siltie
- Gordena Sera of Kestane Gurage
- Kitcha: The Gurage Customary Law (Published in 1998 by Sebat Bet Gurage)
- Gordena Shengo (Written version of customary law of Kistane/Sodo Gurage)

👉 ባህላዊ ህጎች (Customary Laws) እና አብነቶቻቸው፡
ባህላዊ ህግ ማለት የህብረተሰቡን ስነ-ምግባር እና ግንኙነት የሚመራ ደንብ ነው:: አብዛኞቹ በቃል የሚያዙ ቢሆኑም አንዳንዶቹ በጽሁፍ ተዘጋጅተዋል (ምሳሌ፡ Kitcha የጉራጌ፣ Gordena Shengo የኪስታኔ ጉራጌ)::

💡 Exam Hint: የብሔሮችን ባህላዊ ህግ ስም ማዛመድ በፈተና ላይ ይበዛል! (Sera ➡️ Sidama, Dere Woga ➡️ Gamo, Seera Addaa ➡️ Oromo, Gordena Sera ➡️ Kestane Gurage)::

Component 2: Council of Elders
The second important institution. Embraces highly respected and well-experienced community members who have detailed knowledge of customary laws and personal qualities such as truthfulness, impartiality, and experience. Elders serve voluntarily without payment. The number of elders varies based on case nature.
• Different Names for Council of Elders:
- Yehager Shimagile (Amhara)
- Jaarsaa Biyyaa (Oromo)
- Baliqenet (Siltie)
- Hayyicha (Gedeo)
- Guurtii (Somali)
- Dere Cima (Gamo)
- Deira Cima (Wolayita)
- Cimuma (Burji)

👉 የሀገር ሽማግሌዎች ምስራቅና ስያሜዎቻቸው፡
የሀገር ሽማግሌዎች ያለ ክፍያ በፈቃደኝነት ያገለግላሉ:: በተለያዩ ብሔሮች የተለያዩ ስሞች አሏቸው (ምሳሌ፡ Yehager Shimagile፣ Jaarsaa Biyyaa፣ Baliqenet፣ Guurtii ወዘተ)::

Component 3: Customary Courts
Public assemblies that serve two major purposes: (a) hearing, discussing, examining, and settling disputes, and (b) revising, adapting, and making laws.
• Case Study - Gamo Customary Justice System Structure:
1) Dere Woga (Customary laws)
2) Dere Cima (Council of elders)
3) Dubusha (Customary courts/assemblies: guta dubusha ➡️ sub-dere dubusha ➡️ dere dubusha)
- Sacredness of Dere dubusha: Believed to be a sacred place where supernatural power exists, justice is delivered, and truth prevails. Misconduct (lying) brings transgression of taboos and misfortunes.

👉 ባህላዊ ችሎቶች (Customary Courts)፡
ጉዳዮችን ለመመርመር፣ ለመወሰን እና ህግ ለማሻሻል የሚያገለግሉ የህዝብ አደባባዮች ናቸው:: በጋሞ ባህል Dubusha የተቀደሰ ቦታ ስለሆነ ውሸት መናገር መከራና እርግማን ያመጣል ተብሎ ይታመናል::


CHARACTERISTIC FEATURES, STRENGTHS & LIMITATIONS OF CUSTOMARY JUSTICE SYSTEMS

Common Features:
• High involvement of elders at different stages of peacemaking.
• Preference and respect for elders known for impartiality, honesty, listening, speaking politely, and tolerance.
• Focus on restoring social relationships, harmony, and peaceful coexistence.

Differences Across Cultures:
• Differ in terms of hierarchies, procedures, and level of complexity.
• Council compositions and responsibilities vary (some have specialized elders for different disputes; others use the same body).

Strengths of Customary Justice Institutions:
• Incur limited cost in terms of time and resources/money (elders serve without pay; fines are small).
• Process held in public spaces; decisions communicated publicly with wide community participation.
• Decisions easily enforced through community-based sanctions (including social exclusion, blessings, and threat of curses).
• Aimed at restoring community cohesion, social relations, and collective spirit.
• Rely on traditional respect, forgiveness, and compensation.

Limitations of Customary Justice Institutions:
• Limitations regarding women's rights: Dominated by men. Council of elders is not open to elderly women; women are excluded from participation with few exceptions.
• Limitations in inter-ethnic conflicts: Effective within the same ethnic group (intra-ethnic), but potential in resolving inter-ethnic conflicts and restoring long-lasting peace is very limited.

👉 የባህላዊ ፍትህ ስርዓት ጥንካሬና ድክመቶች፡
• ጥንካሬዎች፡ ዝቅተኛ ወጪ፣ ፈጣን ውሳኔ፣ በማህበረሰብ ማግለል (Social exclusion) እና በእርግማን/ምርቃት ህጉ በቀላሉ መከበሩ፣ እና ትኩረቱ በማስታረቅ ላይ መሆኑ::
• ድክመቶች፡ የሴቶች መገለል (በወንዶች ብቻ የተያዘ መሆኑ) እና በሁለት የተለያዩ ብሔሮች መካከል የሚነሱ ግጭቶችን (Inter-ethnic conflicts) የመፍታት አቅሙ አነስተኛ መሆኑ::


6.2.2: INTER-ETHNIC CONFLICT RESOLUTION INSTITUTIONS

Although indigenous institutions have limitations in resolving inter-ethnic conflicts, there are notable examples of inter-ethnic conflict resolution institutions in Ethiopia:

• Abbo Gereb: Indigenous dispute resolution institution in Rayya and Wajirat district, Southern Tigray. Literally means \"father of the river Gerewo.\" Serves to settle disputes between highlanders of Tigray and lowlanders of Afar (often over grazing land or water resources in dry seasons). Notable elders from Tigray and Afar come together to resolve disputes and restore peaceful relations. Most elders involved are bilingual (speaking Tigrigna and Afar) (Shimeles and Taddese 2008).
• Other Regional Names for Inter-Ethnic Conflict Resolution Mechanisms:
- Xinto: among the Afar
- Edible: among the Issa
- Gereb: among the Tigrayans
- Aboroge: among the Amhara (Alula and Getachew, 2008).

👉 የብሔር-በ-ብሔር ግጭት አፈታት (Inter-Ethnic Institutions)፡
• Abbo Gereb: በደቡብ ትግራይ (ራያና ወጅራት) በትግራይና በአፋር ህዝቦች መካከል በግጦሽ መሬትና በውሃ ምክንያት የሚነሱ ግጭቶችን የሚፈታ ባህላዊ ስርዓት ነው:: ሽማግሌዎቹ ሁለት ቋንቋ (ትግርኛ እና አፋርኛ) ይናገራሉ::
• ሌሎች ስሞች፡ Xinto (አፋር)፣ Edible (ኢሳ)፣ Gereb (ትግራይ)፣ Aboroge (አማራ)::

💡 Exam Hint: Abbo Gereb የማንና የማንን ግጭት ይፈታል? 👉 Tigray highlanders & Afar lowlanders! Aboroge የማን ነው? 👉 Amhara!
